episode_title: Partner marketing in B2B: insights from experts at SAP and Accordion

real_qa.q: How many customer touchpoints are required to close a B2B deal at SAP today compared to when Alexandra joined?
real_qa.r: When Alexandra joined SAP, it was 12 touches required to close one deal. At the moment, it's 40 plus touches. This growth means it's not enough to build just one successful marketing activity—companies must work with partners to build the whole customer journey.
real_qa.requete: SAP customer touchpoints deal close 40 plus

real_qa.q: What was the pipeline multiplier effect from SAP's joint co-marketing webinar with partners versus a standard webinar?
real_qa.r: SAP generated 20 times the normal webinar pipeline from a joint co-marketing webinar where both SAP and partners collaborated equally. The key was using a joint target list from previous events and having the inside sales team directly call attendees who had already shown interest in related solutions.

real_qa.q: What specific KPI failures caused SAP's multi-partner campaign with 10 partners to generate zero or minimal leads in September?
real_qa.r: Three problems emerged: telemarketing agencies focused on making calls rather than generating qualified leads; performance marketing campaigns tracked only clicks instead of registrations; and partner brand awareness mattered more than adding 'AI' to activity names. The campaign had zero leads from some performance marketing efforts and minimal results from telemarketing despite active paid media support.
real_qa.requete: SAP 10 partners campaign zero leads KPI failures

real_qa.q: What is Deb's definition of effective partner marketing versus traditional co-branding in B2B?
real_qa.r: Effective partner marketing is not simply putting two logos together on collateral. The real value is finding the intersection between what the partner is trying to achieve, what your company wants to achieve, and absolutely what customers need—starting with a clear business objective like entering a new account, creating demand for a solution, or expanding within an existing account.
real_qa.requete: partner marketing definition B2B intersection customer need

real_qa.q: How far ahead does SAP plan its partner marketing initiatives and detailed partnership activities?
real_qa.r: SAP plans one year ahead and sets final priorities with key activities by end of October or beginning of November. However, real detailed planning on the partners' side is typically for half a year ahead, as market conditions change rapidly, though the goal is to move toward longer-term planning.
real_qa.requete: SAP partner marketing planning horizon one year

guest.bio_context: Alexandra has spent nine years in B2B marketing at SAP, starting as a regional marketer covering a couple of countries and expanding to a bigger region. She has a B2C background and previously worked as a Customer Marketing Manager at a manufacturer doing joint activities with retailers, which introduced her to partner marketing practices.

real_quote: Partner marketing isn't just getting leads and submitting those leads to sales saying we've generated X amount of leads—it's more handshaking and handholding at every step by step.
key_stats: SAP customer touchpoints required: 12 when Alexandra joined, 40+ at present (increase of 233%)
SAP Sertinya campaign reach: 18,000+ targeted contacts from different accounts
Joint co-marketing webinar pipeline multiplier: 20 times normal webinar pipeline
Multi-partner SAP initiative: 10 partners involved, launched September, generated zero leads from some performance marketing campaigns
Partner marketing planning horizon at SAP: One year ahead with final plan by end of October/beginning of November; detailed partner planning: six months
